paragraphs: [Menachot 69b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.69b.5-6) relates that wheat came down for him (from the clouds), a kyuba high over three parasangs.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman prints כיובא (kyuba). The linked Gemara reads כיזבא (kizba) and gives Adi the Arabian as an example in the discussion of wheat that fell from the clouds.

The linked Davidson English gives one handbreadth. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Menachot.69b.6.1) explains the height as “(two) handbreadths with the thumb extended,” with “two” in parentheses in the linked edition.
